rows.what the ink shows: The short abbreviation begins with a long open f-like loop returning upward into a closely joined tall b/l body, then ends with a separate small raised t-shaped hook. It is a contracted abbreviation, with no continuous full-word baseline after the tall cluster.

Above and below the cancellation survive the initial rounded d bowl and upright, a detached i dot, a small low s turn, and a pronounced q descender. After that descender the short connected humps and raised accent precede the final low e stroke, supporting disquée despite the line through its body.

The deletion line covers almost the whole first word; only a few small lower bumps remain. In the second word a triangular tall stroke and several low bowls survive, but the line merges the central connections. The inserted Une trace above is legible, but its lettering cannot establish the deleted phrase below. Retain the deleted phrase uncertainty.

The deleted word retains the tall initial f stroke and its closed descending loop, a low connector through the middle, a later upward t stem and adjacent detached i dot, then a short low terminal on stroke. The uncancelled fonction immediately to its right has the same order of tall f, compressed middle, t and dotted i.

The first word is crossed by two near-coincident heavy strokes; an initial looped upright, further upstrokes, a downward stroke and a crossed tall stem survive, but their intervening letter joins do not securely give positivement. The following homogène is clearer: a tall hooked h, successive rounded humps, a pronounced g descender, a raised accent and low final ne remain distinguishable. Narrow the uncertainty to the first word.

The deleted relation has a distinct upper diagonal sloping down to a right-pointing vertex and a lower arm returning left. To its right is a single closed oval zero. The heavy lower horizontal continues into the zero as part of the cancellation; no separate original equality bar can be distinguished.

Several small initial e/s-like curls and a tall loop near the end project above the scribbled cancellation, with a low final curl. The middle is overdrawn into irregular zigzags, and separate t, dotted i and the full l sequence cannot be recovered securely at 4×. Essentielle is compatible with the skeleton but remains uncertain.

The crossing line hides the word baseline. A very short early upward tick, a low central diagonal return and a late upright with a small open bowl below survive, but the e/x/i/s connections are merged with the cancellation. The clear existe in the rewritten line below supplies a visual comparison but does not recover the deleted word’s missing joins.

The relation has a visible leftward angle and a long lower arm, but several heavy diagonal strokes fill the interior and upper half. A separate equality bar cannot be isolated from that overwritten mass; the same page’s clear ≤ signs have a distinct lower dash. The obscured upper layers leave < and ≤ unresolved.

After the deleted finie there is one short hooked letter with a detached raised abbreviation mark, followed by a tall descending f and the low linked strokes and dots of finie. There is no intervening e-m-i sequence or hyphen as in the expanded semi-finie candidate. The same short form recurs at M0313.

The surviving beginning has a single narrow tall loop rising directly from its entry stroke, followed by a separate lower upright/hump. There is no low oval preceding the tall ascender that would distinguish d; the visible sequence is l then e. The later baseline strokes merge with the cancellation, but they do not obscure this initial le. A targeted reinspection after an independent reading confirmed these components.

Before dense, the abbreviation begins with a long descending f stroke and narrow return, then a compact lower loop beneath a second rising stroke, and a final steep upright/return. These small connected components are compressed but visible above and apart from the underline; they support the abbreviated fblt without expanding it.

In the right-hand cancelled formula, the initial capital A retains two sloping sides, followed by an open curved membership sign, then a calligraphic A with a low oval return and upright right stem. A small raised horizontal-and-upright stroke is present above its right side, supporting the superscript plus. The cancellation crosses these letters but leaves their outlines readable.

The page-edge phrase shows the same single small hooked s with a detached abbreviation stroke as M0309, then a separate tall f, a dot, a low extended joining stroke, and the final dotted/curved strokes of finie. It does not contain the additional letters of semi-finie.
At the right edge after finie, a capital T retains a long top bar and descending stem. An angled/curved cancellation crosses its middle, while the top bar and main stem remain distinct.

The word before fermé has a large hooked initial group, a low extended joining stroke, an oblique terminal stem and a smaller raised crossed stroke consistent with an abbreviated final t. The middle is compressed into the long joining line, and I cannot independently recover all the letters of uniformt from it.
